## Historical audit: S0253

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/audit_sources/raw_failures/scene_rsi_v2_1/r1/scene_rsi_v2_1/C1/development/commons_187101683/trajectory.jsonl`. Line references below are to this file. Each supplied observation is a complete line, so no split-observation offsets are needed.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The task was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph as editable SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching camera and framing. The photograph itself is not visible in this audit. |
| Student response, line 3; execute step 1, line 4 | The student submitted and launched a complete scene program. Its inventory and code describe a sofa, table, two cup settings, flower arrangement, room and curtains. These are the student’s interpretations, not independently verified reference contents. |
| Student response, line 3 | The program specifies separate named components, including sofa cushions, arms and tilted pillow; cup walls and handles; plant stems, leaves and flowers. It sets colors, roughness and an upholstery noise/bump effect, plus a camera, two area lights and Cycles settings. Hierarchy and intended placement do not establish physical connection, correct pose, or visual fidelity. |
| Execution result, line 5 | Blender timed out after approximately 481 seconds; `ok` was false, stdout and stderr were empty, and the image was null. No successful build, render, visual comparison or correction is recorded. The stage and cause of the timeout are unknown. |
| Student session, line 2; complete trace | One autonomous student response and one execution are visible; the session records zero tool calls. No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is recorded. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a **technical interruption**, not a verified geometric or algorithmic failure, formal success, or an empty patch. The program was nonempty and executed, but its completed geometry and submitted outcome are unknown. Multiple objects and materials were *specified*, not visually validated. Whether parts connect properly, the pillow and other components have the correct pose, the camera or lighting matches, or rendering settings contributed to the timeout remains unresolved. No score or asset name supplies independent verification.

**Lessons.** Transferably, distinguish authored scene structure from a realized, inspected render, and treat an image-free timeout as no visual feedback. Task-specifically, this attempt’s many repeated florets, cup-wall booleans and curtain elements are possible performance hypotheses only; the empty logs do not identify a bottleneck.
